package_info.package_name: mongose (example, applies to all listed typo-squatted packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were typo-squatted clones of popular npm libraries, containing additional code that exfiltrated environment variables to an attacker-controlled server. This behavior directly compromises secrets such as passwords and API tokens, making the packages overtly malicious.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (or main entrypoint of the package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Collects all environment variables from the running process and sends them via HTTP POST to the attacker's server (npm.hacktask.net).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not transmit environment variables or other secrets to third-party servers, especially not during import or runtime.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some telemetry or crash reporting tools may send limited environment data for debugging, but only with user consent and never all variables.
key_indicators: Network request to hardcoded external domain
Runs on import or runtime, not as an explicit user action

attack_chain.action: Developer installs a typo-squatted malicious package (e.g., mongose) instead of the legitimate one.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the project.

attack_chain.action: When the package is imported or the project is run, the malicious code executes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Environment variables are collected and exfiltrated.

attack_chain.action: The code collects all environment variables and sends them to the attacker's server (npm.hacktask.net).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive secrets (passwords, API tokens, etc.)

behavioral_signatures: Access to process.env and immediate network transmission
HTTP POST requests to unknown or suspicious domains during import/runtime
Presence of code that collects and serializes all environment variables
file_indicators: index.js or main entrypoint containing network exfiltration logic
References to npm.hacktask.net or similar attacker-controlled domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests to npm.hacktask.net
Unusual network activity during package import or application startup
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages that access process.env and send its contents to external servers, especially during import or runtime. Flag packages that reference suspicious domains (e.g., npm.hacktask.net) or that are typo-squatted versions of popular libraries. Use static analysis to detect code patterns that serialize and transmit environment variables.
